transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what's been bothering you or what brings you in today?

Um, I think… it’s mostly that I’ve been having a harder time explaining myself lately. I’m an artist, so I know I can be a little abstract sometimes, and I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but my artist statements and client notes have been kind of jumping around.

Like I’ll start talking about textures, then suddenly budgets, then what something “means” in a way that feels connected to me, but other people say they can’t follow it. It’s started happening in meetings too, and people keep asking me to slow down or clarify. I guess I’m here because it’s becoming noticeable, and I don’t want it to affect my work more than it already has.
Have you noticed any periods recently where you felt unusually energetic, upbeat, or needed less sleep than usual?

Yeah… I mean, a little. I wouldn’t want to make it sound dramatic, because sometimes I’m just working late and I get into a flow.

But there have been nights where I sleep maybe two or three hours, and then I wake up feeling kind of bright, like ready to keep going. Not really tired the way I normally would be. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you had any recent periods where your mood was notably high, irritable, or unusually upbeat for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least a week?

I think… yes, probably. I don’t want to overstate it, but there are stretches where I feel really lit up, like almost unstoppable, and every idea seems brilliant or important.

And then, it’s not all positive exactly, because if a collaborator makes even a small comment or critique, I can snap more sharply than I mean to. It feels bigger than the situation afterward. Does that count as what you’re asking?
When you feel 'lit up' or unstoppable, does it last long enough that other people notice a change in you, or that it affects your daily activities in a significant way?

Yes… I think people do notice, though I try to keep it professional. It’s more like I get really lit up and almost unstoppable, and every idea feels brilliant or meaningful.

And then if someone says something small, like a collaborator questioning part of it, I can snap more than I mean to. Not in a huge dramatic way, but bigger than the situation really deserves. So… yeah, I guess it does affect things sometimes.
Have you ever had a period where your mood was so high or you were so full of energy that it led to hospitalization, or caused serious problems in your work or relationships?

I haven’t been hospitalized for it, no.

The “serious problems” part is… harder to answer. I’d like to say it’s just creative intensity, but it has caused issues. I’ve missed paid deadlines, and in meetings I think I’ve confused collaborators because my ideas or notes weren’t coming across clearly. There was also an exhibition that got postponed because my notes and proposals kind of stopped making enough sense to use.

I’m not proud of that. I don’t know if that’s what you mean by serious, but it has affected my work and people around me.

Can you tell me if there was a time when this 'lit up' or unstoppable feeling lasted for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least a week? During that time, did it feel like your mood was consistently higher or more irritable than usual, even when you weren’t working or interacting with others?

Yes… I think there have been stretches like that. I don’t want to make it sound more dramatic than it was, but for days in a row I’d wake up already feeling kind of lit up, like I was on and everything I thought of had this really important quality to it.

And it wasn’t only when I was working with people. Even by myself, it could feel like my mood was just… higher than my normal baseline, or more charged. Then if someone made even a small comment, especially a collaborator, I could get irritable fast and snap more sharply than I meant to. Afterward I’d think, okay, that reaction was bigger than the situation. Does that fit what you’re asking?

Can you think of a specific time when this feeling of being 'lit up' or unstoppable lasted for a whole week or more, where it seemed to be there most of the day, nearly every day, even when you weren’t working or interacting with others?

Yes… I can think of a stretch like that, though I’m not sure I could give you exact dates.

It was about a week, maybe a little more, where I woke up already feeling kind of charged, like I was “on” before anything had even happened. It wasn’t just during work or when I was around people. Even alone, I felt lit up, like every idea had this brilliant or important quality to it.

And I tried to frame it as productive or creative, because that sounds better, I guess. But then a small comment from a collaborator could set me off, and I’d snap in a way that was… bigger than the situation really called for. Not constant yelling or anything like that, but definitely more irritable and intense than my usual self. Does that answer it clearly enough?

During that week or more when you felt 'lit up' or unstoppable, did you also notice at least three other changes in your behavior or thinking — like talking more than usual, racing thoughts, being easily distracted, having a lot of goal-directed activity, or doing things that were out of character and had risky consequences?

Yes… I think the main thing I noticed was I’d become very, um, activated around projects.

Like I’d suddenly take on three proposals at once, decide the studio needed to be completely reorganized, start sketching late into the night, email curators, and then begin cutting materials for pieces I hadn’t even really budgeted for yet.

At the time I told myself it was just momentum, or being ambitious, which sounds better. But looking back, it was a lot more than my usual pace. I don’t know if that counts as the kind of “goal-directed activity” you mean?
During that time when you felt 'lit up' or unstoppable, did you also notice things like your thoughts racing, being easily distracted, or taking risks that were out of character for you?

Yes… the racing thoughts part, definitely. I mean, I might have called it “creative flow” at the time, because that feels less worrying, but it could get kind of hard to keep up with.

My mind would jump really fast between images, titles for pieces, grant language, color combinations, conversations I needed to have… like they were all stacking on top of each other before I could even finish one idea. It wasn’t always unpleasant, exactly, but it was a lot. Does that make sense as what you mean by racing thoughts?

Can you recall if there was ever a time when this elevated or irritable mood lasted for at least 4 days in a row, without fading, and it felt clearly different from your usual self, not just a temporary burst of energy or creativity?

Yes… I think so. I mean, I hesitate because part of me wants to call it just a good creative stretch, but it was more than a burst.

There have been times where for several days in a row, at least four, I’d wake up feeling kind of lit up already, like I was unstoppable or like every idea I had was important. And it didn’t really fade the way normal excitement does.

It also came with this edge to it… like if someone I was working with made even a small comment, I could snap back harder than I meant to. It felt bigger than the situation. So yes, I think it was clearly different from my usual self. Does that answer what you mean?
